name: South Carolina Long Term Care Ombudsman
organization: Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman, South Carolina Department on Aging
description: Advocacy for residents of nursing homes and assisted living (community residential care) facilities. Regional ombudsmen work out of the ten Area Agencies on Aging; the state line connects you to them.
next_step: Call 800-868-9095 and give the facility name and county. You can also ask your Area Agency on Aging for the regional ombudsman. To report abuse of an adult living in the community, call 888-227-3487. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.

source_evidence.title: SC Department on Aging: Long Term Care Ombudsman Program

name: South Carolina Department on Aging and GetCareSC
description: The state aging agency. Its toll-free line routes callers to the right regional Area Agency on Aging and Aging and Disability Resource Center for meals, transportation, in-home care, caregiver support and assessment. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call 800-868-9095 from anywhere in South Carolina and give the county where help is needed. Choose a county above for the direct number of its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

name: South Carolina Legal Services (LATIS intake)
description: Free civil legal help statewide for South Carolinians with low income, including housing, public benefits and consumer problems. Not criminal defense.
next_step: Call 888-346-5592 (803-744-9430 in Richland and Lexington counties), Monday to Thursday 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., or apply online at sclegal.org. Have your county and the legal problem ready.
constraints: Income, case type and capacity limits apply. Intake may be paused or limited at times; ask about current intake.

name: VA medical centers serving South Carolina
description: VA medical centers in South Carolina: Wm. Jennings Bryan Dorn VA Medical Center, Columbia VA Health Care System (803-776-4000), with clinics in Anderson, Florence, Greenville, Orangeburg, Rock Hill, Spartanburg and Sumter; Ralph H. Johnson VA Medical Center, Charleston (843-577-5011), with coastal clinics including Myrtle Beach and Beaufort. Some border counties are served by VA systems in Augusta, Georgia or Charlotte, North Carolina.
next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic and its medical center. Not enrolled yet? Call 877-222-8387 or ask your County Veterans Affairs Office for help applying.
constraints: VA does not publish county lists for these systems, so this card does not assign counties. Your VA care team may be at a different clinic or system; follow what VA tells you.

source_evidence.scope: Medical center names and phones; search excerpt.
